questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The two methylene ($-\text{CH}_2-$) protons in ethanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) are stereochemically classified as
questions.explanationEn: Replacing one $-\text{CH}_2-$ hydrogen of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ with deuterium gives $(R)$-1-deuterioethanol, whereas replacing the other gives $(S)$-1-deuterioethanol (a pair of enantiomers). Hence the two protons are enantiotopic.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: For an isolated saturated ketone such as acetone, the electronic transition appearing at the **longest** wavelength ($\lambda_{\max} \approx 279\text{ nm}$, weak intensity $\varepsilon \approx 15\text{ L mol}^{-1}\text{ cm}^{-1}$) is
questions.explanationEn: In saturated carbonyls, the non-bonding oxygen lone pair ($n$) lies highest among occupied orbitals and $\pi^*$ is the LUMO. Thus $n \to \pi^*$ has the smallest energy gap (longest $\lambda_{\max}$) and is symmetry-forbidden (low $\varepsilon$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of carbonyl stretching frequency ($\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$) among acetyl chloride, ethyl acetate, acetone, and acetamide is
questions.explanationEn: Typical $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$ values: acid chloride ($\sim 1800\text{ cm}^{-1}$, strong $-I$ of $\text{Cl}$) $>$ ester ($\sim 1735\text{ cm}^{-1}$, $-I$ of $\text{OEt}$) $>$ ketone ($\sim 1715\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ amide ($\sim 1650\text{--}1680\text{ cm}^{-1}$, strong $+M$ resonance donation from $\text{NH}_2$ lowers $\text{C=O}$ bond order).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following carbocations is the **most** stable in solution?
questions.explanationEn: In the cyclopropylmethyl carbocation, the bent $\sigma$-orbitals (Walsh orbitals) of the strained cyclopropane ring overlap strongly with the vacant $2p$ orbital of the adjacent $\text{CH}_2^+$ carbon ($\sigma$-conjugation), giving exceptional stabilization comparable to benzylic carbocations.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Among the following planar, fully conjugated cyclic species, the one that is **antiaromatic** is
questions.explanationEn: Cyclopentadienyl cation is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and has $4\pi$ electrons ($4n$ with $n = 1$), making it antiaromatic. Tropylium ($6\pi$), $\text{C}_5\text{H}_5^-$ ($6\pi$), and $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8^{2-}$ ($10\pi$) are all aromatic.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Upon progressive dilution of a solution in $\text{CCl}_4$, the broad IR $\text{O–H}$ stretching band of *p*-nitrophenol shifts to a sharp peak near $3610\text{ cm}^{-1}$, whereas the $\text{O–H}$ band of *o*-nitrophenol near $3240\text{ cm}^{-1}$ remains virtually unchanged. This difference arises because
optionsEn: *p*-nitrophenol forms a stronger intramolecular hydrogen bond than *o*-nitrophenol.
*p*-nitrophenol does not contain a phenolic hydroxyl group.
*o*-nitrophenol forms an intramolecular hydrogen bond unaffected by dilution, whereas *p*-nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds that dissociate on dilution.
questions.explanationEn: Intermolecular H-bonding (as in *p*-nitrophenol) is concentration-dependent and breaks upon dilution to yield free $\text{O–H}$ ($\sim 3610\text{ cm}^{-1}$). Intramolecular H-bonding (6-membered chelate in *o*-nitrophenol) is concentration-independent.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following carbon-centered free radicals is the **most** stabilized by resonance delocalization?
questions.explanationEn: The triphenylmethyl radical (Gomberg's radical) delocalizes the unpaired electron across all three phenyl rings (10 resonance structures) and is also sterically shielded against dimerization, making it far more stabilized than benzyl, allyl, or *tert*-butyl radicals.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: $N,N$-Dimethyl-2,6-dimethylaniline is significantly **more basic** than $N,N$-dimethylaniline in aqueous solution because
optionsEn: the *ortho*-methyl groups exert a strong $-I$ effect.
the two *ortho*-methyl groups strongly hydrogen-bond to water around the neutral amine.
protonation relieves hyperconjugation in the aromatic ring.
steric hindrance from the two *ortho*-methyl groups twists the $-\text{NMe}_2$ group out of the benzene plane, preventing lone-pair delocalization into the ring (steric inhibition of resonance).
questions.explanationEn: In $N,N$-dimethyl-2,6-dimethylaniline, steric clash between the *ortho*-$\text{CH}_3$ groups and the $-\text{NMe}_2$ methyls rotates the nitrogen lone pair orthogonal to the aromatic $\pi$-system. Inhibiting resonance makes the lone pair more localized and available for protonation.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Using Woodward–Fieser rules, the calculated $\lambda_{\max}$ for a heteroannular conjugated diene (base value $214\text{ nm}$) having $3$ alkyl/ring-residue substituents ($+5\text{ nm}$ each) and $1$ exocyclic double bond ($+5\text{ nm}$) is
questions.explanationEn: By Woodward–Fieser rules: $\lambda_{\max} = 214\text{ (heteroannular base)} + 3(5)\text{ (3 substituents)} + 5\text{ (1 exocyclic double bond)} = 234\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: At $25\ ^\circ\text{C}$, the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of $N,N$-dimethylformamide ($\text{HCON(CH}_3)_2$) displays **two separate** methyl singlets near $\delta\ 2.88$ and $\delta\ 2.97\text{ ppm}$ which coalesce into a single peak at $120\ ^\circ\text{C}$. This observation is due to
optionsEn: partial double-bond character of the amide $\text{C–N}$ bond from lone-pair delocalization, restricting rotation at room temperature.
tautomerism between the amide and imidic acid forms.
hydrogen bonding between the two methyl groups.
questions.explanationEn: Amide resonance ($\text{O=CH–NMe}_2 \leftrightarrow {^-}\text{O–CH=N}^+\text{Me}_2$) gives the $\text{C–N}$ bond substantial double-bond character (barrier $\sim 85\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). At $25\ ^\circ\text{C}$, rotation is slow on the NMR timescale so the *cis* and *trans* methyl groups give two distinct singlets; heating accelerates rotation past coalescence.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following five-membered heterocycles is/are **aromatic** with $6\pi$ electrons?
questions.explanationEn: Thiophene, oxazole, and thiazole are all planar, fully conjugated $6\pi$-electron heteroaromatic rings (the heteroatom $\text{S}$ or $\text{O}$ contributes one lone pair to the $\pi$ sextet, while the pyridine-like $=\text{N}-$ lone pair stays in an $sp^2$ orbital). Tetrahydrofuran is saturated and non-aromatic.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about qualitative tests for amines is/are correct?
optionsEn: Primary aliphatic and aromatic amines give foul-smelling isocyanides in the carbylamine test ($\text{CHCl}_3/\text{KOH}$).
In the Hinsberg test, a primary amine yields a sulfonamide soluble in aqueous $\text{KOH}$ that precipitates upon acidification.
Tertiary amines do not react with $\text{PhSO}_2\text{Cl}$ to form sulfonamides and dissolve in dilute aqueous $\text{HCl}$.
Secondary amines give a positive carbylamine test.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are standard behaviors of primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. Only primary amines give the carbylamine test, so (D) is false.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) comparing enantiomers and diastereomers is/are correct?
optionsEn: Enantiomers have identical boiling points, melting points, and solubilities in achiral solvents.
Diastereomers generally have different melting points, solubilities, and $^1\text{H}$ NMR chemical shifts in achiral solvents.
Enantiomers rotate plane-polarized light by equal magnitudes in opposite directions under identical conditions.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are true. (D) is false because *cis*- and *trans*-but-2-ene (or *meso*-tartaric acid relative to $(2R,3R)$-tartaric acid) are diastereomers that can be achiral and optically inactive.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compound(s) reduce(s) Tollens' reagent ($[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$) to give a silver mirror?
questions.explanationEn: Aliphatic aldehydes (propanal), aromatic aldehydes (benzaldehyde), and formic acid (which contains an aldehydic $\text{H–C(=O)}-$ unit) all reduce Tollens' reagent to metallic silver. Simple ketones like acetone do not.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of signals observed in the proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum of 1,2-dimethylbenzene ($o$-xylene) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Due to the $C_2$/$\sigma$ symmetry bisecting C1–C2 and C4–C5, $o$-xylene has $4$ chemically distinct carbon environments: (1) two $-\text{CH}_3$ carbons, (2) C1/C2, (3) C3/C6, and (4) C4/C5.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The index of hydrogen deficiency (degree of unsaturation) of an organic compound with molecular formula $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{11}\text{NO}_2$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The index of hydrogen deficiency (degree of unsaturation) of $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{12}\text{ClN}$ is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Halogens count like hydrogens: $\text{IHD} = C - \frac{H + X}{2} + \frac{N}{2} + 1 = 10 - \frac{12 + 1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} + 1 = 5$.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of hyperconjugable $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms in 2-methylbut-2-ene ($(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CHCH}_3$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Three methyl groups are attached directly to the $\text{C=C}$ double bond carbons, contributing $3 \times 3 = 9$ $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms.

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The number of signals observed in the $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum of pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Pentan-3-one is symmetric about the carbonyl group, giving $2$ signals: one triplet ($6\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_3$) and one quartet ($4\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_2$).

questions.pyqTag: IIT JAM CY Topic • Organic Chemistry I: Basic Concepts, Stereochemistry & Spectroscopy (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When $100\text{ mL}$ of a $0.20\text{ M}$ solution of optically pure $(R)$-lactic acid is mixed with $100\text{ mL}$ of a $0.60\text{ M}$ solution of *racemic* lactic acid, the enantiomeric excess ($\text{ee}$) of the resulting solution is _______ $\%$. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Moles of pure $(R)$ added $= 0.100 \times 0.20 = 0.020\text{ mol}$. Moles of racemic added $= 0.100 \times 0.60 = 0.060\text{ mol}$ ($0.030\text{ mol }(R) + 0.030\text{ mol }(S)$). Total $(R) = 0.050\text{ mol}$, total $(S) = 0.030\text{ mol}$, total $= 0.080\text{ mol}$. Thus $\text{ee} = \frac{0.050 - 0.030}{0.080} \times 100\% = 25\%$.
